tagline: AI calendar and task scheduler that auto-plans your workday.
verdictSummary: A greedy auto-scheduler for your own tasks — read calendar availability, pack tasks into free slots by deadline and priority, write the plan back as calendar events — is a real weekend build. What doesn't come with it is robust conflict handling across multiple calendars, team scheduling, and the years of edge-case polish behind 'just replan when something changes.'
coreLoopDIY: A scheduler that reads your calendar's free/busy time, packs your tasks into available slots by deadline and priority within working hours, and writes the result back as clearly labeled calendar events.
whatYouLose: years of polish behind smooth automatic rescheduling
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay because the calendar stays organized without manual drag-and-drop — the automation has to be trustworthy enough to hand off to, which is mostly an edge-case problem, not an algorithm problem.
notes: A good kinda: the core scheduling algorithm is doable, the ongoing automation promise is the real product.
prompt:
Build a personal task auto-scheduler: tasks have a title, a duration estimate, a deadline, and a priority. Read your calendar's free/busy time for the next couple of weeks through its API, respecting configured working hours and a lunch block. Use a straightforward greedy algorithm — earliest deadline first, weighted by priority — to pack tasks into free slots, splitting anything long into smaller chunks. Write the resulting plan back as calendar events clearly marked as machine-created (a prefix in the title is enough), and make replanning delete and recreate only those marked events — never touch a real meeting. Surface overdue or unschedulable tasks visibly rather than silently dropping them. Run this on a schedule each morning so the plan stays current.

Do not build team scheduling, mobile apps, or meeting-invite handling — this plans your own solo work around a calendar it treats as read-only truth, and that's the honest, complete scope.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Motion tasks?
faq.a: Not automatically — Motion doesn't offer a structured export of its task list. Recreating an active task list by hand is realistic, since most people don't carry a large backlog of scheduled items.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: The scheduled plan shows up as normal calendar events, visible on any calendar app on your phone. Adding or editing tasks, though, needs the small web page or CLI, not a mobile-native flow.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting and a database, typically a few dollars a month — the calendar API itself is free at personal usage volumes.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Graceful handling of a busy, changing calendar. Motion's rescheduling has been tuned against years of real conflicts and edge cases; a greedy algorithm here works well for a fairly calm calendar and gets rougher the messier your week actually is.
